channel.title: Iñaki Sobera — Blog
channel.description: Technical notes by Iñaki Sobera on applied AI, MCP and RAG.

item.title: A repo that updates itself with Banxico's data
item.description: Banxico al Día collects 22 Banco de México indicators every business day with a GitHub Action. The git history ends up being Banxico's publication history.

item.title: I sent a patch to the Linux kernel and it got accepted
item.description: It was 15 deleted lines in a staging driver, but Greg Kroah-Hartman accepted it and it's now in linux-next.

item.title: How I connected Claude to Mexico's central bank
item.description: AI assistants don't know what the dollar is worth today. That's how mcp-banxico was born, my MCP server that now gets over 1,700 downloads a month.

item.title: Gordito, my agent that lives in the terminal (and plays music)
item.description: I wanted an agent that worked on my machine without sending my files to any API. That's how Gordito was born, on Ollama, with tools, MCP and a Tux that changes faces.

item.title: My first PR merged into a project that isn't mine
item.description: I added deny rules to MCP Guard, a security scanner for MCP servers. It closed an open issue and got merged the same day.

item.title: Explaining embeddings with a 3D map (because I had to understand them too)
item.description: Two repos I built to learn RAG in public. A visual embeddings explorer and an end-to-end tutorial on the Pagila database.

item.title: My first MCP, or how I talked to SQL Server in plain Spanish
item.description: The MCP Relational AI Gateway was my first contact with the Model Context Protocol. Ask your database in natural language and it draws the chart.

item.title: The day I started a RAG system for PEMEX
item.description: How Xerebro was born, the assistant that reads the refineries' daily reports. The first week was all about fixing things I didn't know could break.

item.title: From school assignments to object detection with YOLO
item.description: How my GitHub started. Spoiler, with a text comparer, a coffee machine and a whole lot of Java.
